citation: Mohammed Latif Siddiq et al. (2024). Using Large Language Models to Generate JUnit Tests: An Empirical Study. EASE '24: Proceedings of the 28th International Conference on Evaluation and Assessment in Software Engineering. doi:10.1145/3661167.3661216
dataset: HumanEval bản Java (160 lớp, lời giải Java do tác giả viết) và EvoSuite SF110 (194 lớp, 47 dự án)
setting: Zero-shot sinh JUnit5; nhiều kịch bản ngữ cảnh trong prompt (HumanEval 3 kịch bản, SF110 4 kịch bản)
metric: Tỉ lệ biên dịch, correctness, coverage, test smells
main_result: HumanEval: dưới một nửa test của Codex (2K, 4K) và GPT-3.5-Turbo biên dịch được, StarCoder 70%; sửa heuristic tăng tỉ lệ biên dịch trung bình 41% (Codex 2K từ 37,5% lên 100%). SF110: chỉ 2,7%-12,7% biên dịch được. Codex trên 80% coverage ở HumanEval, không mô hình nào quá 2% ở SF110; test có smell
limitations: Lời giải Java chuẩn cho HumanEval do tác giả tự viết (mối đe doạ nội tại); mô hình đời cũ; test sinh zero-shot
rq_relevance: Rất cao: HumanEval, JUnit, đo tỉ lệ biên dịch trực tiếp; bài seed

citation: Jaskeerat Singh et al. (2026). A Qualitative and Quantitative Exploration of LLM-Based Test Generation Repair Loops. FSE Companion '26: Proceedings of the 34th ACM International Conference on the Foundations of Software Engineering. doi:10.1145/3803437.3804438
tool_llm: GPT-5-mini (test hỏng ban đầu sinh bởi ChatUniTest)
dataset: 3 dự án Java: Commons-CLI (88 test sửa), Apple-BPG (44), Event-ruler (35); tổng 167 cặp test hỏng-đã sửa
setting: Vòng sửa tối đa 5 lượt với prompt zero-shot, few-shot, chain-of-thought; phân tích tay 117 cặp
metric: Tỉ lệ biên dịch thành công sau sửa (repair rate), coverage sau sửa, phân loại anti-pattern
main_result: Tỉ lệ biên dịch: CLI 97,7% / 98,9% / 97,7% (0-shot / few-shot / CoT); ER 40,0% / 88,6% / 45,7%; BPG 88,6% / 90,9% / 86,4%. Coverage gần như không đổi giữa các kiểu prompt. Phát hiện 31 anti-pattern trong 117 cặp; phổ biến nhất là phá vỡ đóng gói (reflection), sau đó là sai đối tượng và đổi hành vi mong đợi
limitations: Bài ngắn 3 trang (FSE Companion); một mô hình; tác giả nêu sẽ đánh giá toàn diện hơn sau
rq_relevance: Rất cao: vòng sửa theo phản hồi, tỉ lệ biên dịch theo kiểu prompt, test Java

citation: Alex Chudic et al. (2026). Automated Test Suite Enhancement Using Large Language Models with Few-shot Prompting. ICPC '26: Proceedings of the 2026 34th IEEE/ACM International Conference on Program Comprehension. doi:10.1145/3794763.3794828
dataset: HumanEval và ClassEval (Python); 1.754 test do LLM sinh cho HumanEval, 1.259 cho ClassEval; ví dụ viết tay và ví dụ sinh bởi Pynguin (SBST)
setting: Few-shot 5 ví dụ; nguồn ví dụ là người viết, SBST hoặc LLM; chọn ví dụ theo độ tương đồng (retrieval)
metric: Compilation correctness, syntactic correctness, pass rate, coverage, chất lượng mã
main_result: Ví dụ viết tay cho coverage và correctness tốt nhất; chọn ví dụ theo độ tương đồng kết hợp mô tả bài và code cho prompt hiệu quả nhất; thí nghiệm sơ bộ: số ví dụ (1, 3, 5) không đổi tỉ lệ test biên dịch được, riêng pass rate tăng ở ví dụ viết tay khi dùng 5 ví dụ
limitations: Python (không phải Java/JUnit); chỉ một mô hình (GPT-4o); HumanEval gồm bài đơn giản

citation: Aminata Diop et al. (2025). From Scenario to Code: Structured Prompting for LLM-Based Unit Test Generation. WSSE '25: Proceedings of the 2025 7th World Symposium on Software Engineering. doi:10.1145/3779657.3779658
tool_llm: Mistral 7B (prompt hai bước zero-shot: sinh kịch bản test rồi sinh mã test)
dataset: SBST 2020: 70 lớp Java chọn lọc (20 từ GUAVA, 20 từ FESCAR, 20 từ PDFBOX, 10 từ SPOON)
setting: Prompt có cấu trúc 2SZSP, so sánh với EvoSuite
metric: Coverage, mutation score, độ dễ đọc
main_result: Coverage thấp hơn EvoSuite nhưng test dễ đọc, đúng ngữ cảnh hơn và mutation score cao hơn. Khoảng 64% test sinh ra không dùng được (không biên dịch hoặc không hợp lệ)
limitations: 64% test không dùng được; lớp được chọn qua lọc vì giới hạn thời gian; mô hình 7B nhỏ, không phải ChatGPT/Gemini
rq_relevance: Cao: prompt có cấu trúc (khớp RQ), Java, báo tỉ lệ test không biên dịch

citation: Asta Slotkienė et al. (2026). A Formal Trustworthiness Construct for Large Language Model-Based Test Generation: A Multidimensional Index Empirically Evaluated Through a Multi-Agent Study. Electronics. doi:10.3390/electronics15163694
tool_llm: Nhiều LLM; cấu hình tốt nhất kết hợp prompt với Gemini
dataset: Phương thức C# thật; 18 cấu hình (mô hình x prompt) cùng baseline do người viết
setting: Hệ đa agent tự sinh, build, sửa và đo test; chỉ số tin cậy T-UTG gồm độ tin cậy, kháng hallucination, maintainability, đầy đủ chức năng, độ khớp với test người
metric: Chỉ số T-UTG (entropy weighting; phân tích rank-acceptability)
main_result: Baseline người đạt T-UTG 0,904; cấu hình tốt nhất (Combined x Gemini) 0,788; hai chiều phân biệt mạnh nhất là maintainability và kháng hallucination
limitations: Chỉ xét theo abstract (chưa có toàn văn); ngôn ngữ C#
rq_relevance: Cao: có Gemini, có baseline người và bước repair

citation: Zhiqiang Yuan; Mingwei Liu; Shiji Ding; Kaixin Wang; Yixuan Chen; Xin Peng; Yiling Lou (2024). Evaluating and Improving ChatGPT for Unit Test Generation. https://doi.org/10.1145/3660783
dataset: 1,000 Java focal methods from Maven projects selected from CodeSearchNet; separate 100-pair ChatTester evaluation
setting: Empirical study and user study; initial test generation followed by iterative refinement; separate repair evaluation repeated three times
metric: Syntactic correctness; compilation correctness; execution correctness; coverage; assertions; readability; usability
main_result: Initial study: 42.1% compilation success, 24.8% execution success, 57.9% compilation errors and 17.3% execution failures. Separate ChatTester evaluation: compilation 39.0% to 73.3% (+34.3 percentage points), execution 22.3% to 41.0% (+18.7 percentage points).
code_available: Paper cites https://github.com/FudanSELab/ChatTester/tree/main; current accessibility not independently verified
limitations: No Gemini comparison or frozen 30-problem HumanEval design; iterative refinement differs from exactly one repair round; initial-study and repair-evaluation denominators differ
rq_relevance: Direct evidence for compilation/execution failure metrics, assertion failures and compiler-feedback repair

citation: Zejun Wang; Kaibo Liu; Ge Li; Zhi Jin (2024). HITS: High-coverage LLM-based Unit Test Generation via Method Slicing. https://doi.org/10.1145/3691620.3695501
tool_llm: HITS; GPT-3.5-turbo-0125; ChatUniTest; ChatTester; SymPrompt; EvoSuite
dataset: Complex Java methods with cyclomatic complexity > 10 from 10 open-source projects; groups before and after the training cutoff
setting: Static dependency extraction, method slicing, per-slice generation, self-debugging and post-processing; up to 10 repair rounds
metric: Line coverage; branch coverage; test pass rate; test count
main_result: Average line/branch coverage exceeds the studied baselines. High test pass rates do not necessarily imply high coverage.
code_available: Paper cites https://anonymous.4open.science/r/SlicePromptTest4J-6CF1/; current accessibility not independently verified
limitations: Coverage-focused, multiple repair rounds, no Gemini comparison; Markdown contains placeholder ACM year/conference/DOI, so collected 2024 metadata is retained
rq_relevance: Direct Java evidence for complexity-related test generation challenges; supports considering branching/loop complexity when designing task categories

citation: Gabriel Ryan; Siddhartha Jain; Mingyue Shang; Shiqi Wang; Xiaofei Ma; Murali Krishna Ramanathan; Baishakhi Ray (2024). Code-Aware Prompting: A Study of Coverage-Guided Test Generation in Regression Setting using LLM. https://doi.org/10.1145/3643769
dataset: 897 focal methods challenging for SBST from open-source Python projects
setting: Regression test generation using TreeSitter-derived approximate path constraints and focal context; multi-stage prompts per execution path
metric: Correct test generation ratio; code coverage
main_result: CodeGen2 correct generations improve approximately fivefold and relative coverage increases by 26%; GPT-4 relative coverage increases by 105% over baseline prompting.
code_available: Paper describes a proprietary prototype with public release under review; current code availability not independently verified
limitations: Python rather than Java/JUnit; coverage-focused; multiple prompts; no direct Gemini comparison or exactly-one-round repair evaluation
rq_relevance: Indirect evidence for structured prompting and branching complexity; useful methodological background, not a direct JUnit execution comparison

citation: Gu, Siqi; Zhang, Quanjun; Li, Kecheng; Fang, Chunrong; Tian, Fangyuan; Zhu, Liuchuan; Zhou, Jianyi; Chen, Zhenyu (2024). TestART: Improving LLM-based Unit Testing via Co-evolution of Automated Generation and Repair Iteration. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2408.03095

setting: Generation-repair co-evolution, template-based repair, coverage feedback and positive prompt injection; Java 1.8/JUnit 4; up to four iterations, three repetitions
metric: Compilation/execution/pass rates; line/branch/mutation coverage; assertion/test counts; cost
main_result: Markdown reports 78.55% pass rate on Defects4J and 90.96% line coverage on focal methods with passing tests, with approximately 18% pass-rate and 20% coverage improvements over baselines.

citation: Lin Yang; Chen Yang; Shutao Gao; Weijing Wang; Bo Wang; Qihao Zhu; Xiao Chu; Jianyi Zhou; Guangtai Liang; Qianxiang Wang; Junjie Chen (2024). On the Evaluation of Large Language Models in Unit Test Generation. https://doi.org/10.1145/3691620.3695529
tool_llm: CodeLlama-7B-Instruct; CodeLlama-13B-Instruct; Phind-CodeLlama-34B-v2; DeepSeekCoder-6.7B-Instruct; DeepSeekCoder-33B-Instruct; GPT-4; EvoSuite
dataset: 778 public focal methods involving 413 defects in 17 Defects4J 2.0 projects; original benchmark contains 835 defects
setting: Empirical comparison of prompt descriptions, code features and in-context learning; AST-based extraction; JaCoCo; compilation-error test methods recursively removed for coverage collection
metric: Compilation Success Rate (CSR); line coverage; branch coverage; Number of Detected Defects (NDD)
main_result: Prompt design affects performance. Studied LLMs, including GPT-4, achieve lower coverage than EvoSuite. On average, 87.13% of defects cannot be tested for detection because of compilation issues; this is a defect-level percentage, not a test compilation failure rate.
code_available: Paper cites https://github.com/LeonYang95/LLM4UT; current accessibility not independently verified
limitations: No direct Gemini comparison; removing failing test methods differs from retaining unmodified AI output; does not implement the frozen HumanEval/one-repair-round design
rq_relevance: Direct evidence for CSR measurement, compilation failures and the influence of prompt/context choices

citation: Konstantinou, M., Degiovanni, R., Zhang, J. M., Harman, M., & Papadakis, M. (2025). YATE: The Role of Test Repair in LLM-Based Unit Test Generation. arXiv:2507.18316.
dataset: 6 real-world Java projects; 393 classes under test / test-generation problems; 3,657 methods under test
setting: CoT initial generation + compilation fixing + oracle fixing + coverage augmentation; class- and method-level generation
metric: Compilation rate; passing rate; line/branch coverage; mutation score; number of LLM requests
main_result: YATE compilation: 94.60% class-level and 90.02% method-level vs 88.64%/84.34% for plain LLM. Passing: 90.18%/82.96% vs 50.53%/53.40%. Compilation fixing is the most important component in the ablation study.
code_available: Not independently verified in this synthesis
limitations: Different projects/models from our planned HumanEval-Java experiment; YATE uses multi-step repair rather than exactly one repair round.
rq_relevance: Very high: direct evidence that compilation feedback and context-rich repair improve LLM-generated test runnability.

citation: Chen, J., Wang, Z., Yang, L., et al. (2026). Context Matters: Improving the Practical Reliability of LLM-Based Unit Test Generation (Experience Paper). arXiv:2607.19682.
tool_llm: Multiple state-of-the-art LLMs; context-aware CATGen pipeline
dataset: 8 proprietary Java projects with 183 focal methods + Defects4J
setting: Structured context retrieval + deterministic test scaffolding + program-analysis post-processing
metric: Compilation success rate; passing rate; line/branch coverage; time/token cost; mutation analysis
main_result: Compilation failure remains a major adoption barrier. CATGen improves compilation robustness by explicitly providing project dependencies and deterministic post-processing rather than relying only on iterative prompting.
code_available: Industrial/proprietary parts are not fully public
limitations: Java-focused; industrial benchmark; open-weight pipeline setting differs from interactive ChatGPT/Gemini conditions.
rq_relevance: Very high: supports dependency/context and scaffolding as failure-category factors and motivates separating runnability from coverage.

citation: Pan, R., Kim, M., Krishna, R., Pavuluri, R., & Sinha, S. ASTER: Natural and Multi-language Unit Test Generation with LLMs. arXiv:2409.03093.
dataset: Java SE/EE projects (Apache Commons, CargoTracker, DayTrader, PetClinic, App X) + 283 Python modules
setting: Static-analysis-guided generation; compile/runtime checks; rule-based fixes; compiler-feedback re-prompting
metric: Line/branch/method coverage; naturalness; developer survey; compilation/runtime remediation
main_result: Static-analysis-guided LLM generation is competitive with traditional generators on coverage and explicitly performs compilation/runtime repair before evaluation.
code_available: Paper describes tool/pipeline; availability not independently verified here
limitations: Broad multi-language/coverage focus; not a controlled ChatGPT-vs-Gemini HumanEval comparison.
rq_relevance: High: supports compile/run validation, context enrichment, compiler-feedback repair, and broader test-quality distinction.
